findings.text: Local APIC interrupt chip wiring exposes edge acknowledge, affinity control, message composition, forced move completion and retrigger operations under a single controller identity. An alternate build disables affinity and forced completion by defining those hooks as absent.
Edge acknowledge first finalizes any completed vector move for the associated configuration and then acknowledges the interrupt at the APIC level.
Retrigger resends the currently stored vector to the currently stored target processor and reports success unconditionally.
Forced move completion does nothing when chip data is missing, when no previous vector is recorded, or when neither the current nor the previous owner matches the executing processor.

Vector migration retains a previous vector and previous processor while flagged in progress, then releases the old vector through a dedicated free step. Deferred cleanup is scheduled only while the in progress flag remains set, and a timer callback performs the deferred cleanup.
A global vector lock guards chip data lookup and move state inspection, retrigger transmission, deferred cleanup execution, and interrupt matrix accounting during offline feasibility checks.
A public scheduling helper derives chip data from a hardware configuration and requests deferred cleanup only when migration is marked in progress.
A public offline feasibility check counts allocated, available and reserved vectors under lock and refuses CPU removal when available capacity cannot absorb allocated vectors.
Offline refusal uses a no space error when available vectors are fewer than vectors to move, and emits a warning without refusal when reserved vectors exceed available vectors.

Early interrupt controller diagnostics first respect a quiet verbosity setting, then dump legacy controller state, then local APIC state for a configurable processor count when APIC hardware is present, then IO APIC state.

Local APIC diagnostics report identity and version, priority registers, logical and destination configuration, spurious vector, in service and trigger and request bitmaps in fixed size groups, error state with an erratum workaround, interrupt command, timer configuration and extended feature registers when supported.
Legacy controller diagnostics serialize port reads and command writes with the legacy controller lock while preserving interrupt state.
A boot option controls diagnostic breadth with a keyword selecting all processors and a numeric value selecting a bounded prefix, defaulting to a single processor.

Cluster mode keeps a global table mapping processor number to logical identifier plus per processor scratch masks for destination building and per processor shared pointers to cluster membership masks.

Cluster membership is determined by the high bits of the physical identifier. The logical identifier places the cluster number in the upper half and a single bit selected by the low nibble in the lower half.

Cluster mask lifecycle allocates one mask per cluster for the first processor and shares it with present siblings at boot, reuses any surviving mask for late hotplug in a known cluster, otherwise allocates and prefills for newly present siblings, marks the local processor present at loader init, and clears the bit plus frees scratch state at processor death.

Clustered mask delivery copies the caller mask to per processor scratch, optionally removes the caller, then emits one logical interrupt per represented cluster by ORing member logical identifiers and removing the whole cluster from further consideration.

Cluster probe runs only when clustered mode is active, allocates the logical identifier table sized for cache efficiency and processor count, registers processor prepare and death handlers, and initializes the local membership loader.

Cluster controller selects logical destination mode, enables offline non maskable delivery, provides cluster specific probe, loader, identifier calculation and mask delivery, and uses MSR based register access with native end of interrupt and command handling.

Physical mode can be forced by a boot parameter, can be required by firmware revision plus a physical flag, gates table compatibility on mode availability plus either selection source, and probes successfully when forced or firmware required or already selected.

Physical delivery addresses each target processor individually using its stored physical identifier, skips the caller for the all but self mask variant, uses shorthand hardware broadcast for all and all but self, uses a direct self interrupt for self delivery, and treats identifier translation as identity.

Physical controller selects physical destination mode, enables offline non maskable delivery, provides physical probe and per target and shorthand delivery, and uses MSR based register access with native end of interrupt and command handling.
Secure AVIC state is a per processor page sized byte array with page alignment, accessed as bitmaps at register offsets, with helpers to set or clear an individual vector bit at a chosen offset.

Secure AVIC register reads serve timer and local vector entries through a secure channel, serve identity and control and error and extended entries from local memory, serve service and trigger bitmaps only on wide alignment, serve request and allowed request bitmaps on two interleaved strides, and return zero with diagnostics on misalignment or unknown offset.
Allowed request bitmap base offset is decimal five hundred sixteen.
Secure non maskable request register offset is decimal six hundred thirty two.

If an old vector has not been cleaned when affinity is reapplied, the later affinity attempt can fail as busy and leave the line stale. Forced completion therefore always frees the moved vector, and warns with interrupt and old vector identities when migration is still flagged during stop machine where normal completion cannot run.

A theoretical race exists where an interrupt raised before reprogramming takes effect arrives on the old vector after cleanup, risking a spurious event or stale line. The observed reasoning treats hotplug as largely safe due to rendezvous behavior with interrupts enabled, leaving only extreme bus delay or virtualization as a residual concern.

Secure register reads treat misaligned service, trigger, request and allowed request offsets as programming errors with a one time warning and zero result, and treat unknown offsets as errors with logging and zero result.
Both clustered and physical mask delivery issue a special fence for extended APIC registers and preserve local interrupt state while iterating and transmitting.
